headline: TSMC said demand for server processors used by AI agents keeps rising, and it explained how it thinks about pricing.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear statement from the world's top chip maker; limited detail was readable.
importance_line: It signals that AI spending is reaching ordinary server processors, not only graphics chips, but TSMC gave no figures and said US-made chips will be priced differently.
summary: Digitimes reports that TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, said at its 15 October earnings briefing that demand for processors tied to AI agents continues to rise. According to a summary of the call transcript, chairman and CEO C.C. Wei also said TSMC sets prices by market segment, location and technology, so chips made in the US will be priced differently.
notes: Digitimes paywall; second sentence draws on BigGo's call summary.
